본 보고서는 전라남도 신안군 압해읍 매화리 일대의 매화도 및 그와 인접한 마산도·황마도를 대상으로, 2024년부터 2025년까지 수행한 해양유산 학술조사의 결과를 종합한 것입니다.

국립해양유산연구소가 2007년 만재도 조사를 시작으로 축적해 온 섬 해양유산조사 사업의 연장선상에서, 매화도 조사는 서해연안해로의 요충지라는 지리적 특성과 압해도·고이도·기점도·병풍도 등과 함께 형성된 서남해 해상네트워크 속 매화도의 역사·문화적 위상을 규명하는데 중점을 두었습니다.

이번 조사를 통하여 매화도·마산도·황마도를 둘러싼 환경·지형·역사·민속·생업·신앙·생애사 자료 등을 통합적으로 제시함으로써, 세 섬이 서해 연안해로의 전략적 거점이자 해양유산의 집적지이며, 농·어업 복합 생업과 세시신앙이 교차하는 ‘섬살이 문명’의 한 유형임을 밝히고자 하였습니다.

resultList.nttCnEn: The National Research Institute of Maritime Cultural Heritage has been carrying out extensive research on shipwrecks since 2008. Investigations on the Taean Treasure ship, a sunken vessel from the Goryeo Dynasty (918–1392), were followed from 2009 to 2011 by research on Mado Shipwrecks No. 1, 2, and 3. Additionally, the the first vessel from the Joseon Dynasty(1392 – 1910), Mado Shipwreck No. 4, was examined in 2015. The Mado waters—referred to as Nanhaengryang (難行梁, literally, “hard to pass bank”) for their rough nature—have long been regarded as one of the top four most treacherous maritime routes in Korea. As the location of numerous shipwrecks, however, these coastal waters have become a treasure trove of maritime cultural history. The discovery of ancient ships has been achieved through prospectings and excavations. This publication is a follow-up report to the earlier published survey report on the Mado waters. It includes detailed information on the prospectings and excavations conducted from 2011 to 2012 and again in 2014.

resultList.nttCnEn: National Research Institute of Maritime Cultural Heritage excavated the underwater excavation of Mado Shipwreck No. 4, From May to November 2015, a ship in the Joseon Period that was buried under the seabed off the coast of Mado Island, Geunheung-myeon, Taean, Chuncheongnam-do. The excavation of this shipwreck revealed various types of artifacts, including buncheong ceramics, wooden tablets, scoop nets and adzes. The remaining timber of Mado Shipwreck No. 4, the first found Joseon shipwreck, measures about 12m long, 5m wide and 2m deep. It has three rows of the bottom planks, four levels on the left side, eleven levels on the right side, two levels on the stern planks, two levels on the bow planks, and garyong beams. After salvaging artifacts from the inside of the timber and investigating the timber structure, the excavation team re-buried this for salvaging it in the future. Mado Shipwreck No. 4 is the first excavated shipwreck sunken in the Joseon Period. The excavated materials of this ship provide significant information to study the issues of shipbuilding technology, economy, culture and porcelain of the early Joseon Period. Comparative studies on the timber of ship and artifacts salvaged from Goryeo shipwrecks and Mado Shipwreck No. 4 will contribute to the research of the diachronic transition pattern of the pre-modern Korean society.

resultList.nttCnEn:
The “Chinese Ceramics Excavated from Waters off the Taean-Mado Area” is a research report on Chinese ceramics discovered during trial excavations and explorations that took place in waters off
Mado Island for four years since 2009. Chinese ceramics excavated in waters off Mado Island had been produced in Fujian Province during China’s Song and Yuan Dynasties and ceramics of similar
style have also been found in Hakata, Kyushu Area in Japan, indicating that they will serve as an important material in understanding exchanges among the three countries of Korea, China and Japan. So far, a total of 166 pieces of Chinese ceramics have been excavated in waters off Mado Island, which vary extensively, ranging from various white porcelains and celadons to black-glazed porcelain and stoneware jars. The bases of some of the ceramics are inscribed with Chinese characters among which “hwan (丸)” and “seon (船)” indicate “vessels or boats,” while the remaining characters refer to family names. The Chinese character “gang (岡),” which comes after the family names, is a contraction of “gangsa (岡司)” meaning large-scale merchant fleets (商團) that were even protected by private military force. This report heralds the launch of a full-fledged research on excavated underwater relics and we plan to publish in-depth research papers on an ongoing basis - not only on ceramics, but also on artifacts made from metal, stone or plant materials.

e National Research Institute of Maritime Cultural Heritage has excavated wreckages of one Goryeo-period vessel every year since 2009 along the coast of Geunheung-myon of Chungchungnam-do’s Taean-gun. Excavation research of Mado shipwreck No.3 in 2011 was the Institute‘s latest endeavor with shipwrecks dating back to the Goryeo period. Structural integrity of the Mado shipwreck No.3 is found to be preserved in its entirety, harboring wooden tablets used as cargo manifest, collection of pottery and celadon vessels and volumes of grains and organic matters. Excavation of artifacts was completed, but the Mado shipwreck No.3 was left to rest underwater to be salvaged in one piece without damage to its structure in 2015. Various artifacts excavated from the Mado shipwreck No.3 further distinguished rich history and culture of the Goryeo period. As were Mado shipwrecks No.1 and No.2, it was the wooden tablets that were instrumental in revealing
the age and historic signicance of the Mado shipwreck No.3. After deciphering 35 wooden tablets, it was revealed that the Mado shipwreck No.3 sunk sometime between 1265 to 1268 en route to Ganghwado, capital city of Goryeo, carrying grain and exotic seafood such as abalones, mussels and sharks collected in Yeosu-hyun region of Jeollanam-do. One recipient of the cargo is identied to be Kim Jun of Goryeo’s military-controlled government, the most powerful man of the time.

resultList.nttCnEn: National Research Institute of Maritime Cultural Heritage has been conducting exploration projects in the waters of Mado, including nanhaengnyang, since 2009, when local fishermen reported the discovery of cultural assets. These exploration projects led to great achievements - the excavation of Mado Shipwerck No.1 in 2009, Mado Shipwerck No.2 in 2010, and Mado Shipwerck No. 3 in 2011. Conducting exploration projects together with underwater excavations in the waters of Mado resulted in the excavation of many relics. Leading relics that were discovered as a result of the exploration projects are stone anchors and pottery wares. Stone anchors have been excavated since 2009. To date, a total 68 stone anchors have been excavated. stone anchors were an essential tool of vessels. The other leading relicis pottery. Various pottery wares were discovered, many of them from dierent eras and areas. Some are from Korea, while others are from China. They were made in dierent eras as proven by the discovery of initial celadon wares and modern ceramic wares. What we should take special note of is the excavation of Chinese ceramic wares with a Chinese character inscription in the bottom, made using black ink. What was inscribed was the family names and written seals of merchants who conducted international maritime trade during the Song and Yuan Dynasties of China. The Goryeo Dynasty actively engaged in maritime trade with China. The excavated pottery wares are proof.
